rules.summary: Clears the interrupt-enable bit (bit 0) of COP0 Status and returns the previous value of that bit; also merges the global interrupt-mask word into Status.
rules.evidence: mfc0 $12 at 0x800052f0, `addiu at,0,-2; and` clears bit 0, mtc0 $12 at 0x800052fc, `andi v0,t0,1` returns the old bit (0x80005300). Reads the word at 0x80006880 (global interrupt mask) before and after. Called by every thread, message and timer routine around their critical sections.

rules.summary: ORs its argument back into COP0 Status (re-enables interrupts when the argument is the bit returned by os_internal_disable_int).
rules.evidence: Seven instructions at 0x80005350: mfc0 t0,$12; or t0,t0,a0; mtc0 t0,$12; nops; jr ra. Always called with the value os_internal_disable_int returned (0x80003190/0x800031b8 in thread creation).

rules.summary: Writes COP0 Status from $a0.
Returns COP0 Status.
Returns the COP0 Count register (CPU cycle counter at half the CPU clock).
rules.evidence: 0x80004f00: mfc0 $v0,$9; jr ra. Used by the time-keeping routines to extend the 32-bit counter to 64 bits.

rules.summary: Writes COP0 Compare from $a0 (arms the timer interrupt).
Returns COP0 Cause.
Writes the FPU control/status register (FCR31) from $a0 and returns the old value.
Returns the FPU control/status register (FCR31).
Replaces the interrupt-mask bits of Status (bits 8-15) and of the MI interrupt mask register from $a0, combined with the global interrupt mask; returns the previous combined mask.
rules.evidence: 0x80003e20: mfc0 $12 (0x80003e20), reads MI_INTR_MASK at 0xA430000C (0x80003e48), the global mask word 0x80006880, builds the return value from both, writes Status back with mtc0 $12 and updates the MI mask. 40 instructions, no calls.

rules.summary: ORs $a0 into the global interrupt-mask word at 0x80006880 inside a disable/restore pair.
rules.evidence: 0x80004f10: os_internal_disable_int; lw 0x80006880; or with a0 (0x80004f38); sw back; os_internal_restore_int.

rules.summary: Clears the bits of $a0 (except bits 0 and 10) from the global interrupt-mask word at 0x80006880 inside a disable/restore pair.
rules.evidence: 0x80005280: os_internal_disable_int; `addiu at,0,-1026; and t8,t7,at` (0x800052a0-0x800052a4) keeps all but bits 0 and 10 of the argument; nor, and with the word at 0x80006880, store back (0x800052b8); os_internal_restore_int.

rules.summary: Four-instruction stub copied to the CPU exception vectors; loads the address of the exception handler into $k0 and jumps to it.
rules.evidence: 0x800025a0: lui k0,0x8000; addiu k0,k0,0x25b0; jr k0 (the target is os_internal_exception). osInitialize copies these words to 0x80000000, 0x80000080, 0x80000100 and 0x80000180.

rules.summary: General exception handler: saves the interrupted thread's registers into its OSThread context, reads Cause (mfc0 $13) and EPC, dispatches on the exception code and on the pending interrupt lines (count/compare, software interrupts, SP, SI, AI, VI, PI, DP through MI_INTR, the cartridge line through the hardware-interrupt table, pre-NMI), sends the event messages registered with osSetEventMesg and finishes in os_internal_dispatch_thread.
rules.evidence: 0x800025b0: 342 instructions. Saves $at,$v0-$v1,$a0-$a3,$t0-$t9,$s0-$s7,$gp,$sp,$fp,$ra,HI,LO into the running thread and Status at +0x118, EPC at +0x11c (mfc0 $14 at 0x80002714), Cause at +0x120 (mfc0 $13 at 0x80002774); FPU registers when the thread flag +0x18 is set (0x8000271c-0x80002770). Exception code = Cause & 0x7c: 0x24 (break) -> 0x80002a40, 0x2c (coprocessor unusable) -> 0x80002b88, 0 (interrupt) -> pending-line loop at 0x800027b0 with a table jump (`jr t2` at 0x800027e0); any other code stops and faults the thread (0x80002aa4). Interrupt lines are acknowledged by writing SP_STATUS 0xA4040010 (0x8008), VI_CURRENT 0xA4400010, AI_LEN 0xA450000C, SI_STATUS 0xA4800018, PI_STATUS 0xA4600010 (2) and MI_MODE 0xA4300000 (0x800), each followed by a call to 0x80002ad4 with an event index. Ends with `j 0x80002d14` (os_internal_dispatch_thread) at 0x80002a84, 0x80002a9c and 0x80002acc.

rules.summary: Part of the exception handler: given an event index in $a0, sends the message registered for that event (table of {queue, message} pairs at 0x8000a410) to its queue if the queue has room, and wakes the first thread waiting on it.
rules.evidence: 0x80002ad4: table base 0x8000a410 plus a0 (0x80002ad8), loads queue->validCount (+8) and msgCount (+16), computes (first+validCount) mod msgCount with div (0x80002b0c), stores the message, increments validCount, pops a waiting thread with the pop routine at 0x80002d04 and enqueues it on the run queue (0x80002cbc); returns with `jr s2` (the caller saved ra in $s2 inside the handler, 0x80002ae4).

rules.summary: Saves the running thread's context (Status|2, resume PC = $ra, callee-saved registers, FPU state when the thread uses it), enqueues the thread on the queue in $a0 when that is non-null, and dispatches the next runnable thread.
rules.evidence: 0x80002bbc: loads the running thread from 0x80006860, mfc0 $12 | 2 stored at +0x118 (0x80002bc4-0x80002bd0), $s0-$s7,$gp,$sp,$fp,$ra at +0x98-+0x100, $ra also as resume PC at +0x11c (0x80002c08), cfc1 $31 and $f20-$f30 saved when thread +0x18 is non-zero (0x80002c04-0x80002c28), folds the global interrupt mask 0x80006880 and MI_INTR_MASK 0xA430000C into +0x118 and +0x128 (0x80002c2c-0x80002ca8); `beq a0,0` skips the enqueue (0x80002ca4), otherwise calls 0x80002cbc; ends with `j 0x80002d14`.

rules.summary: Inserts the thread in $a1 into the linked queue headed at *$a0, ordered by descending priority (field +4), and records the queue in thread +8.
rules.evidence: 0x80002cbc: walks nodes comparing the priority at +4 with `slt` (0x80002ccc, 0x80002ce4) and stops at the first node of lower priority; links the thread in (sw at 0x80002cf4/0x80002cf8) and stores the queue address into thread +8 (0x80002d00). Called by os_internal_enqueue_and_yield (0x80002cac) and osStartThread (0x8000622c, 0x80006270).

rules.summary: Removes and returns the first thread of the queue at *$a0.
rules.evidence: 0x80002d04: lw v0,0(a0); lw t9,0(v0); jr ra; sw t9,0(a0) in the delay slot: head = *q; *q = head->next; return head.

rules.summary: Pops the highest-priority runnable thread from the run queue (0x80006858), marks it running (state 4) and records it at 0x80006860, loads its saved Status/EPC/registers and returns to it with eret; when the queue is empty it installs the idle-thread context.
rules.evidence: 0x80002d14: calls os_internal_pop_thread on the queue at 0x80006858 (0x80002d18), mtc0 $12 and $14 write Status and EPC from the thread context, eret at the end, reads/writes MI_INTR_MASK (0xA430000C) to restore the thread's interrupt mask. The only function with eret.

rules.summary: Unlinks the thread in $a1 from the queue whose head pointer is at $a0.
rules.evidence: 0x80002ea0: walks `p = *q` comparing against $a1 and relinks `prev->next = a1->next` (0x80002ec4 sw t6,0(a2)); one loop, no calls.

rules.summary: Initialises the OSThread in a0: id a1 at +0x14, priority (6th argument) at +4, entry a2 as resume PC at +0x11c, argument a3 in the saved $a0 slot (+0x38/+0x3c), stack top (5th argument) minus 16 as saved $sp (+0xf0/+0xf4), the thread-exit stub 0x80002e90 as saved $ra (+0x100/+0x104), initial Status 0xff03 (+0x118), interrupt mask 0x3f (+0x128), initial FPCSR 0x01000800 (+0x12c), state 1 (stopped); links the thread into the all-threads list at 0x8000685c.
rules.evidence: 0x80003090: `sw` of a1 at +0x14 (0x800030b4), of 60(sp) (the priority) at +4 (0x800030c0), of a2 at +0x11c (0x800030dc), of a3 sign-extended at +0x38/+0x3c (0x800030f0-0x800030f4), of stack-16 at +0xf0/+0xf4 (0x80003118/0x8000311c), of the constant 0x80002e90 at +0x100/+0x104 (0x80003124-0x80003134), Status 0xff03 (0x80003148-0x8000314c), 0x3f at +0x128 (0x80003164), 0x01000800 at +0x12c (0x80003170-0x80003174), state `sh 1,16` (0x80003188) and `sh 0,18` (0x80003194); then os_internal_disable_int (0x80003190), thread->next(+0xc) = *0x8000685c, *0x8000685c = thread (0x800031ac-0x800031bc), os_internal_restore_int. Called by the boot main at 0x80000570 with priority 10.

rules.summary: Starts a thread: a stopped thread (state 1) with no wait queue (or already on the run queue) becomes runnable (state 2) on the run queue 0x80006858; a thread in state 8 is also made runnable; afterwards dispatches when nothing is running, or yields when the head of the run queue outranks the running thread.
rules.evidence: 0x800061e0: state (+0x10) tested against 1 (0x80006208) and 8 (0x8000620c); `sh 2,16` + os_internal_enqueue_thread(0x80006858, thread) at 0x80006224-0x8000622c and 0x80006268-0x80006270; a thread whose queue (+8) is another queue is set to state 8, re-enqueued there and the queue head is popped (os_internal_pop_thread at 0x800062a0) onto the run queue; then reads the running thread 0x80006860: none -> os_internal_dispatch_thread (0x800062cc), else compares priorities (+4) with slt (0x800062f4) and calls os_internal_enqueue_and_yield(0x80006858) after setting the running thread to state 2 (0x80006300-0x8000630c).

rules.summary: Stops the thread in $a0, or the running thread when $a0 is 0: a running thread (state 4) becomes stopped and yields; a runnable (2) or waiting (8) thread is unlinked from its queue and becomes stopped.
rules.evidence: 0x800020d0: a0==0 gives state 4 (0x800020f4-0x800020fc), otherwise state = thread +0x10; switch on 2, 4, 8 (0x80002110-0x80002124); state 4: `sh 1,16(running)` then os_internal_enqueue_and_yield(0) (0x8000213c-0x80002148); states 2 and 8: `sh 1,16(thread)` then os_internal_dequeue_thread(thread->queue (+8), thread) (0x80002158-0x80002168).

rules.summary: Destroys the thread in $a0 (or the running thread when 0): removes it from the queue it waits on (unless stopped) and from the all-threads list at 0x8000685c, and dispatches when it was the running thread.
rules.evidence: 0x80002ee0: os_internal_disable_int; a0==0 selects the running thread 0x80006860 (0x80002f0c); state != 1 -> os_internal_dequeue_thread(thread->queue, thread) (0x80002f20-0x80002f34); unlinks it from the list at 0x8000685c by walking the +0xc links (0x80002f3c-0x80002fa0; the walk ends at a node with priority -1, 0x80002f68); when it is the running thread calls os_internal_dispatch_thread (0x80002fbc); os_internal_restore_int. Also the target of the exit stub 0x80002e90.

rules.summary: Sets the running thread runnable (state 2) and re-queues it behind equal-priority threads.
rules.evidence: 0x80005bc0: os_internal_disable_int; `sh 2,16(running)` (0x80005bd8-0x80005bec); os_internal_enqueue_and_yield(0x80006858); os_internal_restore_int.

rules.summary: Sets the priority (a1) of thread a0 (0 = running thread) and re-sorts it in its queue; yields when the running thread no longer has the highest priority.
rules.evidence: 0x800045e0: os_internal_disable_int; priority stored at thread +4; the thread is dequeued and re-enqueued in its queue; os_internal_enqueue_and_yield on the run queue when needed; os_internal_restore_int. Calls os_internal_dequeue_thread, os_internal_enqueue_thread and os_internal_enqueue_and_yield.

rules.summary: Returns the id field (+0x14) of the thread in $a0, or of the running thread when $a0 is 0.
rules.evidence: 0x80003e00: `bne a0,0; lw a0,0x6860(0x8000)` (running thread); `lw v0,20(a0)`.

rules.summary: Initialises an OSMesgQueue (a0) over the buffer a1 with capacity a2: both wait lists point at the empty-list sentinel 0x80006850, valid count 0, first 0.
rules.evidence: 0x80004380: stores the address 0x80006850 at +0 and +4, zero at +8 and +0xc, a2 at +0x10 (msgCount) and a1 at +0x14 (message buffer); 11 instructions, no calls.

rules.summary: Appends message a1 to queue a0. When the queue is full: returns -1 for a2==0, blocks the caller on the queue's fullqueue (+4) for a2==1 (OS_MESG_BLOCK) and retries. After storing, wakes the first thread waiting in mtqueue (+0).
rules.evidence: 0x80001f80: compares validCount (+8) with msgCount (+0x10) (0x80001fac); blocking path sets running-thread state 8 and calls os_internal_enqueue_and_yield with queue+4 (`addiu a0,a0,4` at 0x80001fe8); stores at msg[(first+validCount) mod msgCount] with div (0x80002038), validCount++ (0x80002078), pops a waiting receiver and calls osStartThread (0x800020a0).

rules.summary: Removes the oldest message from queue a0 into *a1 (if a1 is non-null); when empty, returns -1 for a2==0 or blocks the caller on the queue's mtqueue for a2==1. After removing, wakes the first thread waiting in fullqueue (+4).
rules.evidence: 0x800021a0: validCount==0 test (0x800021c8); blocking path calls os_internal_enqueue_and_yield with queue (0x80002200); copies msg[first] to *a1 (0x80002238-0x8000223c); first=(first+1) mod msgCount with div (0x80002250), validCount-- (0x8000228c); pops a sender from queue+4 (`addiu a0,t9,4` at 0x800022a8) and restarts it.

rules.summary: Inserts message a1 at the front of queue a0 (first = (first+msgCount-1) mod msgCount), blocking like osSendMesg when the queue is full and waking a waiting receiver.
rules.evidence: 0x80004490: same full-queue test and blocking structure as osSendMesg, but writes the message at the decremented `first` index; called by osEPiStartDma (0x80004220) to put a DMA request at the head of the PI command queue.

rules.summary: Registers queue a1 and message a2 for event a0 in the table at 0x8000a410 (8 bytes per event); event 14 additionally touches the global interrupt mask.
rules.evidence: 0x80004110: os_internal_disable_int; index*8 added to 0x8000a410 (0x80004130-0x80004140); stores queue and message (0x80004148, 0x8000415c); compares the event with 14 (`addiu at,0,14` at 0x80004154); calls os_internal_set_global_int_mask for it; os_internal_restore_int.

rules.summary: Installs handler a1 and stack pointer a2 for hardware interrupt a0 in the table at 0x80006620 (8 bytes per entry).
rules.evidence: 0x800064c0: os_internal_disable_int; `sll t8,a0,3` and stores a1/a2 into 0x80006620+index*8 (0x800064ec-0x80006508); os_internal_restore_int. The exception handler loads the table entry at 0x80002824 and calls it with jalr (0x8000283c).

rules.summary: Returns the 64-bit CPU cycle count: the saved total at 0x8000a4b0/0x8000a4b4 plus the cycles elapsed since the count saved at 0x8000a4b8.
rules.evidence: 0x80004a70: os_internal_disable_int; osGetCount; subtracts the saved count (0x80004aa8), reads the total (0x80004a90-0x80004aa4); os_internal_restore_int; 64-bit addition with carry via sltu (0x80004ad0-0x80004af0).

rules.summary: Clears the 64-bit total time, the saved count and the timer list and points the list head at itself.
rules.evidence: 0x80004b00: stores zeros to 0x8000a4b0-0x8000a4bc (total hi/lo, saved count, armed count) and initialises the list words at 0x800068d0; no calls. Called by osCreateViManager (0x80005ee4).

rules.summary: Inserts an OSTimer into the list of pending timers headed at 0x800068d0, ordered by absolute expiry (64-bit compares).
rules.evidence: 0x80004d78: os_internal_disable_int/os_internal_restore_int around two loops over the list; reads the head at 0x800068d0.

rules.summary: Programs COP0 Compare for now + the 64-bit interval in a0:a1 and records the count at which it was armed (0x8000a4c0).
rules.evidence: 0x80004d04: os_internal_disable_int; osGetCount stored at 0x8000a4c0 (0x80004d1c-0x80004d24); count + interval (0x80004d3c-0x80004d54); os_internal_set_compare (0x80004d58); os_internal_restore_int.

rules.summary: Compare-interrupt handler of the timer list: runs expired timers (sending each timer's message to its queue), re-inserts periodic ones and re-arms Compare.
rules.evidence: 0x80004b8c: calls osGetCount, osSendMesg, os_internal_insert_timer, os_internal_set_timer_intr and os_internal_set_compare; reads the list head at 0x800068d0; called from os_internal_vi_mgr_main.

rules.summary: Starts timer a0 for the 64-bit interval a2:a3 (period a4:a5 when non-zero), sending its message to its queue on expiry.
rules.evidence: 0x80005d80: 53 instructions; calls os_internal_insert_timer and os_internal_set_timer_intr only.

rules.summary: Returns the PI manager's command queue (0x80006898) or 0 when the PI manager is not running (flag at 0x80006890).

Posts one PI transfer request to the PI manager: a0 = OSPiHandle, a1 = request record, a2 = direction (0 reads the cartridge, non-zero writes it). Stores the handle at request +0x14, the request type 15 (a2 = 0) or 16 (a2 != 0) at +0, and sends the request to the PI command queue: with osJamMesg at the front when the request byte +2 equals 1, with osSendMesg otherwise. Returns -1 when the PI manager is not running.
rules.evidence: 0x80004220: returns -1 when the PI manager flag 0x80006890 is zero (0x80004224-0x80004248); the store `sw a0,20(a1)` at 0x80004258 stores the handle; the halfword at +0 is 15 when a2 is zero (0x80004268-0x80004274) and 16 otherwise (0x80004278-0x80004280); the byte at +2 selects osJamMesg (0x800042ac) when it is 1, osSendMesg (0x800042d0) otherwise; the queue comes from osPiGetCmdQueue (0x80004298, 0x800042bc). Callers pass the handle first: dma_copy_from_rom at 0x80000a4c (a0 = word at 0x80006730, a1 = request on its stack, a2 = 0) and 0x80091adc.

rules.summary: Converts a virtual address to a physical address: KSEG0/KSEG1 by masking with 0x1fffffff, TLB-mapped addresses through os_internal_probe_tlb; returns -1 when unmapped.
rules.evidence: 0x80003cc0: compares with 0x80000000, 0xa0000000, 0xc0000000 (0x80003cd0-0x80003d0c) and masks with 0x1fffffff; the other case calls 0x80003f30.

rules.summary: Looks up virtual address a0 in the TLB (tlbp), reads the matching entry (tlbr) and returns the physical address, or -1 when there is no valid mapping.
rules.evidence: 0x80003f30: sets EntryHi (mtc0 $10) from the address and ASID, tlbp (0x80003f54), tests Index bit 31, tlbr (0x80003f74), reads PageMask ($5), EntryLo0/1 ($2/$3) and picks the half-page by the address bit.

rules.summary: Invalidates all TLB entries except the wired one(s): writes an invalid EntryHi with tlbwi for indices 30 down to 0.
rules.evidence: 0x800041d0: `addiu t1,0,30` (0x800041d4); loop writing Index ($0), EntryLo0/1 = 0, EntryHi = 0x80000000 with tlbwi (0x800041f0) and decrementing until negative (bgez at 0x80004200).

rules.summary: Writes TLB entry 31 so that virtual 0xC0000000 maps to physical 0 (page mask 0), used for the debugger window.
Writes back (without invalidating) the data-cache lines covering [a0, a0+a1); sizes of 0x2000 or more write back the whole cache by index.
rules.evidence: 0x800035b0: `cache 0x19` (Hit_Writeback_D) in a 16-byte stepped loop (0x800035e8-0x800035f4); size compared with 0x2000 (0x800035b8); `cache 0x01` (Index_Writeback_Invalidate_D) over 0x80000000.. (0x8000360c).

rules.summary: Invalidates the data-cache lines covering [a0, a0+a1), writing back partially covered edge lines first; sizes of 0x2000 or more use an index operation.
rules.evidence: 0x800043b0: `cache 0x15` (Hit_Writeback_Invalidate_D) at 0x800043ec, `cache 0x11` (Hit_Invalidate_D) and `cache 0x01` for large sizes; threshold 0x2000 (0x800043b8).

rules.summary: Invalidates the instruction-cache lines covering [a0, a0+a1); sizes of 0x4000 or more use an index operation.
rules.evidence: 0x80004300: `cache 0x10` (Hit_Invalidate_I) in a 32-byte stepped loop (0x80004338-0x80004340), `cache 0x00` (Index_Invalidate_I) for large sizes; threshold 0x4000 (0x80004308).

rules.summary: Starts one PI DMA transfer: waits for PI_STATUS idle, translates the RAM address, writes PI_DRAM_ADDR, PI_CART_ADDR (device address ORed with the ROM base word 0x80000308) and the length register selected by direction.
rules.evidence: 0x80003bf0: polls 0xA4600010 & 3 (0x80003c08-0x80003c28); calls osVirtualToPhysical (0x80003c2c); stores to 0xA4600000 (0x80003c40); reads 0x80000308 (0x80003c48); also writes 0xA4600004 and the length registers. No callers in the boot image.

rules.summary: Starts a PI DMA like os_internal_pi_raw_start_dma, for an OSPiHandle (a0): first reprograms the domain timing registers from the handle when they differ from the last handle used for the domain.
rules.evidence: 0x80004890: waits on PI_STATUS (0x800048a8-0x800048c8); reads handle fields +4..+9 and compares with the previous handle; writes PI domain registers 0xA4600014-0xA4600030 and the DRAM/CART/length registers 0xA4600000-0xA460000C; one call (osVirtualToPhysical). No callers in the boot image.

rules.summary: Reads one 32-bit word from device address a1 through the PI bus into *a2, after programming the domain timing registers from OSPiHandle a0.
rules.evidence: 0x800046e0: waits on PI_STATUS 0xA4600010 (0x800046e8-0x80004708); domain registers 0xA4600014-0xA4600030 are reprogrammed when the handle differs from the last one (0x80004710-0x80004818); `or t4,t3,0xa0000000; lw t5,0(t4); sw t5,0(a2)` (0x80004828-0x80004838).

rules.summary: Writes the 32-bit value a2 to device address a1 through the PI bus, after programming the domain timing registers from OSPiHandle a0.
rules.evidence: 0x80005c20: same set-up as os_internal_e_pi_raw_read_io (0x80005c20-0x80005d5c), then `or t4,t3,0xa0000000; jr ra; sw a2,0(t4)` (0x80005d68-0x80005d74).

rules.evidence: 0x80001f10: tests the flag at 0x800067c0 (0x80001f14-0x80001f20), calls 0x80001ec0 when clear, then osRecvMesg(0x80008f78, &msg, 1) (0x80001f30-0x80001f40).

rules.summary: Releases the PI bus by sending a message to the access queue.
osPiGetAccess; os_internal_e_pi_raw_write_io; osPiRelAccess.
rules.evidence: 0x80005b10 calls osPiGetAccess (0x80001f10), the raw write os_internal_e_pi_raw_write_io (0x80005c20, at 0x80005b30) and osPiRelAccess (0x80001f54).

rules.summary: osPiGetAccess; os_internal_e_pi_raw_read_io; osPiRelAccess.
rules.evidence: 0x800057e0 calls osPiGetAccess (0x80001f10), the raw read os_internal_e_pi_raw_read_io (0x800046e0, at 0x80005800) and osPiRelAccess (0x80001f54); called by the boot code at 0x800013f4 to read the cartridge header.

rules.summary: Creates the PI manager: the access queue, the command and reply queues, the PI event registration and the PI manager thread (entry os_internal_dev_mgr_main), then starts it.
rules.evidence: 0x80003670: tests the flag at 0x80006890 (the flag osPiGetCmdQueue reads) (0x80003678-0x80003690); calls the access-queue creator 0x80001ec0, osCreateMesgQueue, osSetEventMesg, osCreateThread with entry 0x800037e0, osSetThreadPri, os_internal_disable_int/os_internal_restore_int, osStartThread.

rules.summary: Body of the PI manager thread: loops receiving requests from the command queue, performs them with the raw PI routines, adjusts interrupt masks and replies on each request's queue.
rules.evidence: 0x800037e0: 245 instructions; loops around osRecvMesg (0x80003834) and osSendMesg; one table jump; calls os_internal_e_pi_raw_read_io, os_internal_e_pi_raw_write_io, os_internal_set_global_int_mask, os_internal_reset_global_int_mask and osYieldThread; touches PI_STATUS 0xA4600010.

rules.summary: Initialises the two VI contexts at 0x800068e0 (0x60 bytes cleared), sets the current/next pointers 0x80006940/0x80006944 and selects the default VI mode and origin from the TV type.

rules.summary: Reads or writes save memory: sram_transfer(a0 = cartridge address, a1 = RAM address, a2 = size, a3 = direction 0 read / 1 write). Fills the save-memory PI handle for that address (type 3, latency 5, pulse width 13, page size 2, release 12) with pi_handle_create, then runs sram_pi_transfer.
rules.evidence: 0x80091b14: constants 13, 2, 12 stored as stack arguments (0x80091b28-0x80091b38) and 3, 1, 5 in a1-a3 (0x80091b40-0x80091b48) before pi_handle_create (0x80091b4c); then `jal 0x80091a88` with a1, a2, a3 shifted down (0x80091b54-0x80091b5c). 12 callers in the save-handling code 0x80090c80-0x80091894 pass a0 = 0x08000000 + a table offset (`lui at,0x800` at 0x80090c64 / 0x80090d4c): reads use a3 = 0 (0x80090d58 reads 0x8000 bytes into a buffer cleared with 0x80002ff0), writes use a3 = 1 with size 0x1450 (0x80090c74-0x80090c7c). The 0x08000000 base is the cartridge SRAM window, so saves go through the PI like any cartridge read.
